Rashi on Menachot 2b:11:1.hebrew: קדש קדשים היא וגו' - במנחה כתיב, וקרי לה חטאת ואשם. הא כיצד? מנחת חוטא הרי היא כחטאת, דקי"ל (זבחים דף ב.): כל הזבחים שנזבחו שלא לשמן כשרים, אלא שלא עלו לבעלים לשם חובה, חוץ מן פסח וחטאת שפסולין לגמרי. ובפ"ק דזבחים מפרש טעמא דפסח, ולקמן מפרש טעמא דחטאת:
Rashi on Menachot 2b:11:1.english: It is most sacred, etc. - It is written regarding the meal offering, and [Scripture] calls it a sin offering and a guilt offering. How so? The meal offering of a sinner is like a sin offering, as we maintain (Zevachim 2a): "All slaughtered offerings that were slaughtered not for their sake are valid, except that they do not count for the owner toward fulfilling his obligation, except for the Passover offering and the sin offering, which are completely invalid." And in the first chapter of Zevachim [the Gemara] explains the reason for the Passover offering, and later it explains the reason for the sin offering.

Rashi on Menachot 2b:13:1.hebrew: ואינו מרצה - לא עלו לשם חובה, דבזבחים ר"ש מודה, כדקתני לעיל:
Rashi on Menachot 2b:13:1.english: And it does not effect acceptance - They did not count toward fulfillment of [the owner's] obligation, for with regard to slaughtered offerings Rabbi Shimon agrees, as was taught above.

Rashi on Menachot 2b:13:2.hebrew: אף מנחה כו' - וקשיא דר"ש אדרבי שמעון, בין במנחת חוטא ובין במנחת נדבה:
Rashi on Menachot 2b:13:2.english: So too, a meal offering, etc. - And [this presents] a contradiction between [one statement of] Rabbi Shimon and [another statement of] Rabbi Shimon, both regarding a sinner's meal offering and regarding a voluntary meal offering.

Rashi on Menachot 2b:14:1.english: Here, with a change of sanctity - As I explained above.

Rashi on Menachot 2b:15:1.hebrew: מכדי מחשבה דפסל רחמנא במנחה הקישא הוא - דאיתקיש רחמנא מנחה לזבחים, כדכתיב (ויקרא ו׳:י׳) קדש קדשים היא כחטאת וכאשם. מה זבחים פסלה בה מחשבה, כדכתיב (שם ז) המקריב אותו לא יחשב - אף מנחה נמי, מה לי שינוי קדש ומה לי שינוי בעלים:
Rashi on Menachot 2b:15:1.english: Now consider, [the fact that] the Merciful One disqualified [due to improper] intent in a meal-offering is an analogy - For the Merciful One compared the meal-offering to animal sacrifices, as it is written (Leviticus 6:10): "It is most holy, like the sin-offering and like the guilt-offering." Just as [with] animal sacrifices, [improper] intent disqualifies them, as it is written (ibid. 7): "The one who offers it, it shall not be credited [to him]" — so too [with] a meal-offering as well: what difference is there to me [between] a change of sanctity and a change of owner?

Rashi on Menachot 2b:17:1.hebrew: מחשבה דלא מינכרא - אם מכזב ואם לאו, פסיל רחמנא, דחשיב לה מחשבה:
Rashi on Menachot 2b:17:1.english: An intention that is not recognizable - Whether he is lying or not, the Merciful One disqualifies [the offering], for He considers it an intention.

Rashi on Menachot 2b:17:2.hebrew: אבל מחשבה דמינכרא - לכל שהוא מכזב, לא הוי מחשבה. הך מחשבה דקדשים הוצאת דיבור בפה הוא, כדאמרי' בבבא מציעא (ד' מד.): על כל דבר פשע – לחייב על המחשבה כמעשה, דאי לאו מוציאו בפה, מחשבתו למאי נחייב לה:
Rashi on Menachot 2b:17:2.english: But intent that is recognizable - [That is, recognizable] to all that he is lying, is not [considered] intent. This "intent" regarding consecrated offerings is an utterance of speech with the mouth, as we say in Bava Metzia (page 44a): "For every matter of trespass" — to hold [one] liable for intent like an action; for if he did not articulate it with his mouth, on what [basis] would we hold him liable for his thought?

Rashi on Menachot 2b:19:1.hebrew: אי הכי - כיון דמחשבה הגלויה לכל לא פסלה, עולת העוף כו':
Rashi on Menachot 2b:19:1.english: If so - Since intent that is evident to all does not disqualify, [then] a bird burnt offering, etc.

Rashi on Menachot 2b:19:2.hebrew: עולת העוף - נעשית למעלה מחוט הסיקרא, כדתניא בת"כ: ומלק והקטיר ונמצה — מה הקטרה בראשו של מזבח, אף מליקה בראשו של מזבח; ומיצוי נמי בהאי קרא כתיב. וחטאת העוף למטה, והכי מפרש בשחיטת קדשים בפ' קדשי קדשים (זבחים דף סה.):
Rashi on Menachot 2b:19:2.english: A bird burnt offering - It is performed above the red line, as it is taught in Torat Kohanim: "'And he shall pinch... and burn... and [its blood] shall be drained' — just as burning is on top of the altar, so too pinching is on top of the altar"; and draining [of the blood] is also written in this [same] verse. And a bird sin offering is [performed] below [the red line], and so it is explained in [tractate] Shechitat Kodashim, in the chapter [entitled] "Kodshei Kodashim" (Zevachim 65a).

Rashi on Menachot 2b:19:3.hebrew: תרצה - תעלה לשם חובה, אלמה תנן בשחיטת קדשים בפ' קדשי קדשים (זבחים דף סד:) דלא עלתה:
Rashi on Menachot 2b:19:3.english: It should effect acceptance - It should count toward [fulfilling the owner's] obligation; [yet] why then did we learn in [tractate] Shechitat Kodashim, in the chapter [entitled] "Kodshei Kodashim" (Zevachim 64b), that it did not count?

Rashi on Menachot 2b:1:1.hebrew: ונדבה מי שרי לשנויי בה - והכתיב: אם זבח שלמים קרבנו (ויקרא ג׳:א׳), שתהא זביחה לשם שלמים:
Rashi on Menachot 2b:1:1.english: And with regard to a gift offering, is it permitted to deviate in it? - And is it not written: "If his offering is a sacrifice of peace offerings" (Leviticus 3:1), [teaching] that the slaughtering must be for the sake of peace offerings?

Rashi on Menachot 2b:20:1.hebrew: מליקה - לחטאת העוף בכל מקום במזבח כשירה בפ' קדשי קדשים (זבחים דף סג.), והויא לה מחשבה דלא מינכרא, משום הכי תנן דלא עלתה:
Rashi on Menachot 2b:20:1.english: Pinching - For a bird sin offering, [pinching] anywhere on the altar is valid, [as stated] in the chapter "Kodshei Kodashim" (Zevachim 63a), and [therefore] it is an intent that is not recognizably [false]; for this reason we learned [in the mishna] that it did not satisfy [the owner's obligation].

Rashi on Menachot 2b:21:1.hebrew: עולת העוף - הכשירה במיצוי, דכתיב (ויקרא א): ונמצה דמו על קיר המזבח. חטאת העוף - הזאה תחילה ואח"כ מיצוי, דכתיב: והזה מדם החטאת וגו' והנשאר בדם ימצה וגו' (שם ה):
Rashi on Menachot 2b:21:1.english: A bird burnt offering - Its validation is through draining, as it is written (Leviticus 1): "And its blood shall be drained out on the wall of the altar." [Whereas for] a bird sin offering, sprinkling is first and afterward draining, as it is written: "And he shall sprinkle of the blood of the sin offering, etc., and the rest of the blood shall be drained out, etc." (ibid. 5).

Rashi on Menachot 2b:21:2.hebrew: למטה הוה עביד לה - כדכתי' (שם) על קיר, ומפרש בתורת כהנים: זה קיר התחתון:
Rashi on Menachot 2b:21:2.english: He would have performed it below - As it is written (ibid.): "On the wall," and it is explained in Torat Kohanim: "This is the lower wall."

Rashi on Menachot 2b:21:3.hebrew: הזאה - אוחז בגוף העוף ומעלה ומוריד בכח, והדם ניתז מעצמו. מיצוי - סוחט בין אצבעותיו, ונצוק הדם הולך למרחוק:
Rashi on Menachot 2b:21:3.english: Sprinkling - [The priest] holds the body of the bird and moves [it] up and down forcefully, and the blood spurts out on its own. Draining - He squeezes [it] between his fingers, and the stream of blood travels afar.

Rashi on Menachot 2b:2:1.english: Rabbi Shimon says: All the meal offerings, etc. - And even the meal offering of a sinner.

Rashi on Menachot 2b:3:1.english: For meal offerings are not similar to slaughtered offerings - For regarding slaughtered offerings, I concede that they do not count [toward fulfilling the owner's obligation].

Rashi on Menachot 2b:3:2.hebrew: מעשיה מוכיחים - שהוא מכזב, דמרחשת עמוקה ומעשיה רוחשים, רכין, מחבת צפה ומעשיה קשין, בפרק כל המנחות באות מצה (לקמן מנחות דף סג.):
Rashi on Menachot 2b:3:2.english: Its preparation proves - That he is lying, for a marḥeshet is deep and its product is quivering [and] soft, [whereas] a maḥavat is shallow and its product is hard, [as taught] in the chapter "Kol HaMenachot Ba'ot Matza" (below, Menachot 63a).

Rashi on Menachot 2b:3:3.hebrew: מנחת חריבה - דמנחת חוטא (ויקרא ה׳:י״א) ומנחת קנאות, דכתיב בהו (במדבר ה׳:ט״ו) לא ישים עליה שמן:
Rashi on Menachot 2b:3:3.english: A dry meal offering - For [this refers to] the meal offering of a sinner (Leviticus 5:11) and the meal offering of jealousy, as it is written concerning them (Numbers 5:15): "He shall put no oil upon it."

Rashi on Menachot 2b:3:4.hebrew: בלולה - שאר מנחות. והשתא פליגא מתניתין עליה דר' שמעון בתרתי: חדא, דמתניתין קתני בכל המנחות דלא עלו; וחדא, דקא פסיל תנא דידן מנחת חוטא לגמרי:
Rashi on Menachot 2b:3:4.english: Mixed - [This refers to] the other meal offerings [which are mixed with oil]. And now, our mishna disagrees with Rabbi Shimon on two counts: One, that our mishna teaches regarding all meal offerings that they do not fulfill [the owner's obligation]; and one, that our Tanna completely invalidates the meal offering of a sinner.

Rashi on Menachot 2b:4:1.hebrew: אבל בזבחים אינו כן - אין להם מעשה מוכיח, הילכך מהני בהו שינוי דלא עלו לשם חובה:
Rashi on Menachot 2b:4:1.english: But with slaughtered offerings it is not so - They do not have an action that proves [what they are]; therefore, a change [of intention] is effective in their case, so that they do not count toward [fulfilling the owner's] obligation.

Rashi on Menachot 2b:5:1.hebrew: הניחא לרב אשי - דמתרץ לקמן, כי רמינן דר' שמעון דאמר בדוכתא אחריתי (במתניתין) אדרבי שמעון דהכא, ומתרץ להו רב אשי: דהא דאמר ר' שמעון עלו - באומר: הריני קומץ מחבת לשם מרחשת, דכיון דלא אדכר שמה דמנחה אלא שמה דמנא, דברי רוח בעלמא נינהו; והא דקאמר ר' שמעון בעלמא דלא עלו - כגון דאידכר שמה דמנחה. איכא לאוקומה מתני' כר' שמעון, דמתני' דאידכר שמה דמנח', כדמפר': שלא לשמו ולשמו, לשם מנחת נדבה לשם מנחת חוטא:
Rashi on Menachot 2b:5:1.english: This works out well according to Rav Ashi - Who resolves [this contradiction] later, when we raise a contradiction from [that which] Rabbi Shimon said in another place (in the mishna) against [that which] Rabbi Shimon [said] here, and Rav Ashi resolves them: That that which Rabbi Shimon said, "[and they] satisfy [the obligation]," is where one says: "I am removing a handful from a pan for the sake of a deep-pan," for since he did not mention the name of the meal offering, but only the name of the vessel, they are mere words of wind; and that which Rabbi Shimon says elsewhere, that they do not satisfy [the obligation], is where he mentioned the name of the meal offering. [Therefore,] it is possible to establish our mishna in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, for our mishna is [a case] where he mentioned the name of the meal offering, as it explains: "Not for its sake and for its sake" — for the sake of a gift meal offering, for the sake of a sinner's meal offering.

Rashi on Menachot 2b:6:1.hebrew: אלא לרבה ולרבא - דמשנו לה בטעמי אחריני, כדמפרש לקמן, מאי איכא למימר:
Rashi on Menachot 2b:6:1.english: But according to Rabba and Rava - Who resolve it with other reasons, as [the Gemara] explains later, what is there to say?

Rashi on Menachot 2b:7:1.hebrew: וכי תימא - מתני' מיתוקמא כר' שמעון, כדמשני רבה לקמן לטעמיה דר' שמעון: כאן בשינוי קדש, וכאן בשינוי בעלים. הא דאמר רבי שמעון עלו - בשינוי קדש, כגון מנחת מחבת לשם מנחת מרחשת, דמעשיה מוכיחין שהוא מכזב; והא דאמר לא עלו - בשינוי בעלים, כגון שהביאה ראובן וקמצה כהן לשם שמעון, דליכא מעשה מוכיח אי דראובן היא אי דשמעון:
Rashi on Menachot 2b:7:1.english: And if you would say - [That] the mishna can be established in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, as Rabba resolves later according to Rabbi Shimon's reasoning: "Here [it is] with a change of sanctity, and here [it is] with a change of owner." That which Rabbi Shimon said, "They fulfill [the obligation]," [refers to] a change of sanctity, such as a pan meal offering [sacrificed] for the sake of a deep-pan meal offering, for its mode of preparation proves that he is lying. And that which he said, "They do not fulfill [the obligation]," [refers to] a change of owner, such as where Reuven brought it and a priest removed a handful from it for the sake of Shimon, where there is no action proving whether it belongs to Reuven or to Shimon.

Rashi on Menachot 2b:8:1.hebrew: והא מתניתין בשינוי קדש - מיירי, וקתני דלא עלו, דקתני: כיצד לשמן ושלא לשמן? כגון שקמץ מנחת חוטא לשם מנחת חוטא ולשם נדבה:
Rashi on Menachot 2b:8:1.english: And surely our mishna is with a change of sanctity - [It] is dealing [with this], and [yet] it teaches that they did not fulfill [the owner's obligation]; for it teaches: "How [is it] for their sake and not for their sake?" — for example, where one removed a handful from a sinner's meal offering for the sake of a sinner's meal offering and for the sake of a voluntary [meal] offering.

Rashi on Menachot 2b:9:1.hebrew: ואי נמי כדמשני רבא - לטעמא דר' שמעון: דהא דאמר עלו, בקומץ מנחת מחבת לשם מנחת מרחשת, משום דכתיב "זאת תורת המנחה" (ויקרא ו׳:ז׳), תורה אחת לכל המנחות; והא דקתני לא עלו, בקומץ מנחה לשם זבח. ולקמן פריך: בקומץ לשם זבח לתכשר נמי, דהא "מעשיה מוכיחין עליה" קאמר, ומשני לה לקמן (מנחות דף ג.). והא דנקט לאקשויי במתני' משלא לשמן, ה"ה דמצי לאקשויי לשמן ושלא לשמן, כדאקשינן לרבה, אלא כי סידרא דמתני' נקיט ואזיל:
Rashi on Menachot 2b:9:1.english: And alternatively, as Rava answers - [This explains] the reasoning of Rabbi Shimon: For that which he said, "[they] satisfy [the owner's obligation]," [refers to a case where one] removed a handful from a pan meal offering for the sake of a deep-pan meal offering, because it is written: "This is the law of the meal offering" (Leviticus 6:7) — [teaching that there is] one law for all meal offerings; and that which [the baraita] teaches, "they do not satisfy [the owner's obligation]," [refers to] removing a handful from a meal offering for the sake of a slaughtered offering. And later, [the Gemara] asks: When removing a handful for the sake of a slaughtered offering, let it be valid as well, for doesn't [Rabbi Shimon] say "its actions prove [what] it is"?! And [the Gemara] resolves it later (Menachot 3a). And as for [the Gemara] choosing to raise an objection from the mishna based on [the clause of] "not for their sake [and for their sake]," it could equally have objected from "for their sake and not for their sake," as we objected against Rabba; but it proceeded according to the order of the mishna.

Tosafot on Menachot 2b:12:1.hebrew: מנחת חוטא הרי היא כחטאת - אין זה דבר הלמד בהיקש חוזר ומלמד בהיקש; דאע"ג דחטאת ילפי' למצוה משלמים בפ"ק דזבחים (דף ח.), מכל מקום הא כתיב ביה היא לגופיה לעכב. אבל קשה: הא דיליף מנחת נדבה מאשם דאינו מרצה, ואשם גופיה משלמים ילפינן בפ"ק דזבחים (שם)! וי"ל, דהך דרשא דהכא אסמכתא בעלמא, כדמפרש בזבחים דעיקר קרא לכדר' יהודה בריה דר' חייא [אתי], וילפינן מנחה משלמים בהיקישא דזאת התורה:
Tosafot on Menachot 2b:12:1.english: The meal offering of a sinner is like a sin offering - This is not [a case of] a matter learned through an analogy (hekesh) going back and teaching through an analogy; for even though we derive [the requirement to sacrifice] a sin offering [for its own sake] as a mitzvah [ab initio] from a peace offering in the first chapter of Zevachim (8a), nevertheless, behold, "it" (hi) is written concerning it itself for indispensability [to invalidate it after the fact]. However, it is difficult: That which [Rabbi Shimon] derives a voluntary meal offering from a guilt offering, that it does not effect acceptance — yet the guilt offering itself we derive from a peace offering in the first chapter of Zevachim (ibid.)! And one can say that this exposition here is merely a scriptural support (asmachta be'alma), as is explained in Zevachim (11a) that the primary [purpose of the] verse comes for that of Rabbi Yehuda, son of Rabbi Chiyya; and we derive a meal offering [directly] from a peace offering through the analogy of "This is the law" (Leviticus 7:37).

Tosafot on Menachot 2b:15:1.hebrew: מכדי מחשבה דפסל רחמנא הקישא הוא - דאע"ג דהקישא דכחטאת וכאשם לאו עיקר, מ"מ אתיא בהקישא דזאת התורה. וכיון דהקישא הוא, מה לי שינוי קודש, מה לי שינוי בעלים? וא"ת: מה מקשי אביי לרבה? תיקשי ברייתא גופה, דמוכחא שיש חילוק, מדמפרש טעמא משום דמעשיה מוכיחין! וי"ל: דיכול ליישב הברייתא כהני אמוראי דלקמן. א"נ, קסבר אביי: דכיון דשינוי קודש לא פסול משום דמעשיה מוכיחין, הוא הדין שינוי בעלים, דילפינן משלמים כי ה"ג: דמה שלמים לא חלקת לפסול, אף מנחה לא תחלוק להכשיר; דכי ה"ג דריש תנא דבי חזקיה בפ' אלו נערות (כתובות דף לה.) גבי מכה אדם ומכה בהמה, והך סברא דלא חלק אשכחן בפרק קמא דזבחים (דף ז.) גבי שלמים:
Tosafot on Menachot 2b:15:1.english: Now consider, [the fact that] the Merciful One disqualified [due to improper] intent is an analogy - For even though the analogy of "like a sin-offering and like a guilt-offering" is not primary, nevertheless it is derived via the analogy of "This is the law" (Leviticus 7:37). And since it is an analogy, what difference is there to me [whether it is] a change of sanctity, [or] what difference is there to me [whether it is] a change of owner? And if you say: Why does Abaye challenge Rabba? Let the baraita itself pose a difficulty, as it proves that there is a distinction, since it explains the reason [as being] because its actions prove [its status]! And one can say: That he can resolve the baraita like those Amora'im below. Alternatively, Abaye maintained: Since a change of sanctity does not disqualify because its actions prove [its status], the same applies to a change of owner; for we derive [minchah] from peace-offerings in this manner: Just as regarding peace-offerings you did not distinguish [between types of intent] to disqualify, so too regarding a meal-offering you should not distinguish to validate. For in this manner, the Tanna of the school of Chizkiyah expounded in the chapter "Elu Na'arot" (Ketubot 35a) regarding "one who strikes a person" and "one who strikes an animal"; and this reasoning, that [the Torah] did not distinguish, we find in the first chapter of Zevachim (7a) regarding peace-offerings.

Tosafot on Menachot 2b:19:1.hebrew: עולת העוף שמלקה למעלה - קס"ד, אע"ג דכשירה כחטאת, מכל מקום אין דרך לעשות למעלה, שלא יפול הדם לארץ קודם שיבא למטה למצוה:
Tosafot on Menachot 2b:19:1.english: A bird burnt offering that one pinched above - It entered [the Gemara's] mind that even though it is valid as a sin offering, nevertheless, it is not the practice to perform [it] above, lest the blood fall to the ground before he comes below for the mitzvah [of sprinkling].

Tosafot on Menachot 2b:4:1.hebrew: שחיטה אחת לכולן - לקמן פריך דחלוקים בשחיטתן, דיש בצפון ויש בדרום. והא דלא קתני הולכה אחת לכולן, משום דאיירי הכא אליבא דרבי שמעון, דלא חייש בהולכה בפ"ק דזבחים (דף יד:), משום דהויא עבודה שאפשר לבטלה. ורבי שמעון, דפליג אהילוך בזבח, לא איצטריך לפלוגי בהילוך דמנחות (לקמן מנחות דף יב.); אבל תימה קצת, אמאי לא פליג בקבלה דמנחות, דאיפשר נמי לבטלה לר"ש, כדלקמן פרק הקומץ רבה (מנחות דף כו.): מאי טעמא דרבי שמעון? בא לעובדה ביד, עובדה בימין כחטאת; א"כ, לא בעו קבלה:
Tosafot on Menachot 2b:4:1.english: One [manner of] slaughter for all of them - Later on [3a], [the Gemara] objects that they are divided in their slaughter, as there are [offerings slaughtered] in the north and there are [those slaughtered] in the south. And that which [the baraita] does not teach "one [manner of] conveying for all of them" [is] because here it is speaking according to Rabbi Shimon, who does not take conveying into account [as invalidating through improper intention] in the first chapter of Zevachim (14b), because it is a service that can be eliminated. And since Rabbi Shimon disagrees regarding conveying in an animal sacrifice, he did not need to disagree regarding conveying in meal offerings (later, Menachot 12a). However, it is somewhat puzzling: Why did he not disagree regarding collection of meal offerings, which can also be eliminated according to Rabbi Shimon? As [stated] later in the chapter Hakometz Rabbah (Menachot 26a): "What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon? [If] he comes to perform its service by hand, he performs it with [his] right [hand] like a sin offering" — if so, they do not require collection [in a vessel]!

Tosafot on Menachot 2b:4:2.hebrew: זריקה אחת לכולן - ואע"ג דיש במתנה אחת ויש במתן ארבע, פי' בקונטרס דתנן: אם ניתנו כולן במתנה אחת כיפר. ומיהו קשה: דהניתנין במתן ד' שנתנן לשם ניתנין במתנה אחת לירצו, דמעשיהן מוכיחין כשיתן השניים? וי"ל: דבשעה שנתן הראשונה שלא לשמו עדיין אין מעשיהן מוכיחין עד שיתן האחרון; ובשניה אין מחשבה פוסלת, כדתנן בפ' בית שמאי (זבחים דף לו:) דבמתנה אחת כיפר. אבל קשה מחטאת לשם עולה: דחטאת למעלה, בקרנות ובאצבע, ועולה למטה, ביסוד ובזריקה מן הכלי. ועוד קשה מקבלה: דאשם קבלתו אף בשמאל וחטאת בימין, ואף לרבי שמעון בפ"ב דזבחים (דף כד.) ולקמן בפירקין (מנחות דף י.). ונראה דודאי היה יכול להקשות כן לקמן:
Tosafot on Menachot 2b:4:2.english: One sprinkling for all of them - And even though there are [offerings whose blood is applied] with a single application and there are [those applied] with four applications, the Kuntres [Rashi] explained that we learned [in a mishna]: If they were all placed in a single application, he has effected atonement. However, this is difficult: for those [offerings whose blood is] to be placed with four applications that one applied for the sake of [an offering whose blood is] placed with a single application, let them effect acceptance, for their actions prove [their true status] when he applies the second [applications]! And it can be answered: that at the time he applied the first [application] not for its own sake, its actions do not yet prove [its status] until he applies the last [application]; and during the second [application], [improper] intent does not disqualify, as we learned in the chapter [entitled] "Beit Shammai" (Zevachim 36b), that with a single application he has effected atonement. However, it is difficult from [the case of] a sin offering [applied] for the sake of a burnt offering: for a sin offering is [applied] above [the red line], on the horns [of the altar], and with the finger; whereas a burnt offering is [applied] below, at the base [of the altar], and with sprinkling from the vessel. And furthermore, it is difficult from collection [of the blood]: for [regarding] a guilt offering, its collection [is valid] even in the left [hand], whereas a sin offering [must be collected] in the right [hand] — and even according to Rabbi Shimon in the second chapter of Zevachim (24a) and later in our chapter (Menachot 10a). And it appears that certainly [the Gemara] could have raised such an objection later [as well].
